race_title: Massachusetts ballot, Nov 3 2026: U.S. Senate, Governor

statements.text: Health insurance should be provided through private market competition.

candidatePositions.markey: Markey is the lead sponsor of the State-Based Universal Health Care Act of 2025 and original co-sponsor of Medicare for All Act.

statements.raceInsight: Health care costs remain a top concern for Massachusetts voters, who face some of the highest insurance premiums and out-of-pocket expenses in the nation despite the state's high rate of coverage.
statements.policyBackground: Private health insurance is coverage purchased from commercial insurance companies rather than government programs. Market competition refers to multiple insurers offering different plans, with consumers choosing based on price, coverage, and other factors. Supporters argue this approach encourages innovation and efficiency through competition.

markey.quote: Lead Sponsor: State-Based Universal Health Care Act of 2025 (S.2286) Original Co-Sponsor: Medicare for All Act (S.1506)

statements.text: The United States should transition to 100% renewable, zero-emission energy sources.

candidatePositions.markey: Markey is the Senate author of the Green New Deal, which calls for transitioning the United States to 100% renewable, zero-emission energy sources, zero-emission vehicles, and high-speed rail systems.
candidatePositions.deaton: Deaton opposes the Green New Deal.
candidatePositions.minogue: Mike Minogue plans to cancel the Net Zero mandate, which he says would cost taxpayers over $300 billion.

statements.raceInsight: Energy policy affects Massachusetts residents through electricity bills, gas prices, and climate impacts including coastal flooding and extreme weather events. The state has set ambitious climate goals while residents face rising energy costs.
statements.policyBackground: Transitioning to 100% renewable energy would mean generating all electricity from sources like solar, wind, and hydropower instead of fossil fuels like coal, oil, and natural gas. This would require building new infrastructure, retiring existing power plants, and potentially changing how energy is stored and distributed. Such a transition aims to eliminate greenhouse gas emissions from the energy sector to address climate change.

markey.quote: Markey is the Senate author of the Green New Deal. In February 2019, Markey and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez released a 14-page summary of their Green New Deal plan to address climate change. It calls for implementing the " social cost of carbon " that was part of the Obama administration's plans to address climate change and transitioning the United States to 100% renewable, zero-emission energy sources, zero-emission vehicles, and high-speed rail systems.

deaton.quote: As an independent voice, I will oppose extreme policies like the Green New Deal and support balanced solutions that lower energy costs, protect jobs, and move us toward cleaner, affordable American energy.

minogue.quote: Cancel the unfunded, unachievable Net Zero mandate, which would cost taxpayers over $300 billion.

statements.text: Abortion should be restricted beyond current law.

candidatePositions.markey: Markey opposes restrictions on abortion and wore a pin with the word ABORTION to the 2023 State of the Union Address.
candidatePositions.deaton: Deaton has consistently supported codifying Roe protections into federal law and would switch parties to vote against a federal abortion ban.

statements.raceInsight: Abortion rights are a decisive issue for many Massachusetts voters, particularly following the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision, even though state law currently protects abortion access more broadly than many other states.
statements.policyBackground: Abortion restrictions can include limits based on gestational age, waiting periods, parental consent requirements, or other regulations that make the procedure harder to access. Current Massachusetts law permits abortion throughout pregnancy, with some provisions around viability. Federal law no longer guarantees abortion rights nationwide after the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022.

markey.quote: Since then, he has opposed restrictions on abortion. Markey wore a pin to the 2023 State of the Union Address with the word ABORTION with a heart in place of the central portion of the letter O.

deaton.quote: Since the fall of Roe in 2022, I've consistently supported codifying the protections of Roe into federal law, and I strongly disagree with the Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs. As I said in my last campaign, if national Republicans try to bring a federal abortion ban to the floor (as Attorney General Todd Blanche has promised) I will switch parties and vote with Democrats to stop it.

statements.text: Voters should be required to show identification before casting a ballot.

candidatePositions.deaton: Deaton will fight to protect election integrity through common-sense measures such as free voter identification.

statements.raceInsight: Election security and voter access are debated nationwide, though Massachusetts has not experienced significant documented voter fraud and currently does not require photo ID at polling places.
statements.policyBackground: Voter identification laws require voters to present some form of ID before voting, with requirements varying from strict photo ID to more flexible options like utility bills or signed affidavits. Supporters argue these laws prevent fraud and increase confidence in elections. Opponents contend that fraud is extremely rare and that ID requirements can create barriers for eligible voters who lack required documents, particularly elderly, minority, and low-income citizens.

deaton.quote: I will fight to protect the integrity of our elections through common-sense measures such as free voter identification and transparent processes.

statements.text: Community college should be tuition-free for residents.

candidatePositions.healey: Healey announced a $20 million appropriation to create a free community college program, MassReconnect, for Massachusetts residents 25 or older with a secondary school degree or post-secondary course credits.
candidatePositions.james: James plans to make college education at state schools free.

statements.raceInsight: College affordability affects thousands of Massachusetts families, with student debt burdens impacting young adults' ability to buy homes and build financial security in one of the nation's most expensive states.
statements.policyBackground: Free community college programs eliminate tuition and mandatory fees at public two-year colleges, though students may still pay for books, supplies, and living expenses. These programs aim to increase educational attainment, workforce development, and economic mobility. Funding typically comes from state budgets, and programs may have eligibility requirements based on age, residency, income, or enrollment status.

healey.quote: Healey announced a $20 million appropriation to her 2024 fiscal year state budget proposal to create a free community college program, "MassReconnect", for Massachusetts residents 25 or older with a secondary school degree or post-secondary course credits, to address the skills gap in the state workforce.

james.quote: As Governor, I will expand K-12 community schools that provide comprehensive educational opportunities for all students with on-campus services focused on helping those families who need it, with the resources to be healthy and thriving as their children receive truly the best education in the country, that's not just a deceptive slogan. I will invest in trade schools and high school work study opportunities for students who must work during their high school years, and make college education at state schools free.

statements.text: Local communities should have full control over housing development without state mandates.

candidatePositions.minogue: Minogue plans to eliminate enforcement of the MBTA Communities Act and provide legal support to cities and towns that do not accept its terms.

statements.raceInsight: Housing affordability is the top economic concern for many Massachusetts residents, with median home prices and rents far exceeding national averages. The tension between local zoning control and regional housing needs affects communities statewide.
statements.policyBackground: State housing mandates can require municipalities to allow certain types of development, such as multi-family housing near transit stations or affordable units in new projects. These mandates aim to address housing shortages and affordability by overriding local zoning that may restrict construction. Critics argue they undermine local control and community character, while supporters say regional coordination is necessary to solve housing crises that cross municipal boundaries.

minogue.quote: Eliminate the enforcement of the MBTA Communities Act and provide legal support to cities and towns that do not accept the terms because of their limitations with water, sewer, infrastructure, and school resources.

statements.text: The state should expand publicly funded charter schools.

candidatePositions.minogue: Minogue plans to expand charter, tech, and vocational schools across the Commonwealth.

statements.raceInsight: Education quality and school choice remain contentious issues in Massachusetts, where charter schools have strong supporters and opponents, and where test scores show persistent achievement gaps between districts.
statements.policyBackground: Charter schools are publicly funded but operate independently of traditional school districts, often with different curricula, longer school days, or specialized focuses. They are established through state-approved charters and typically have more flexibility in hiring and operations than traditional public schools. Supporters argue they provide innovation and choice, while critics contend they drain resources from traditional public schools and serve fewer students with special needs.

minogue.quote: Expand charter, tech, vocational schools across the Commonwealth.

statements.text: State and local law enforcement should decline to assist federal immigration enforcement.

candidatePositions.minogue: Minogue plans to prioritize removing violent criminals and drug dealers and end sanctuary state policies.

statements.raceInsight: Immigration policy affects Massachusetts communities with large immigrant populations, raising questions about public safety, civil liberties, and the relationship between state and federal law enforcement.
statements.policyBackground: Sanctuary policies limit cooperation between local or state police and federal immigration authorities, such as by not honoring requests to detain individuals solely for immigration violations or not asking about immigration status during routine interactions. Supporters argue these policies build trust between immigrant communities and police, making everyone safer. Opponents contend they shield dangerous individuals from deportation and undermine federal immigration enforcement.

minogue.quote: At the same time, Mike will prioritize removing violent criminals and drug dealers and end sanctuary state policies.

statements.text: Government should regulate how much landlords can increase rent.

candidatePositions.james: James plans to support rent stabilization policies.

statements.raceInsight: Rising rents force many Massachusetts residents to spend more than half their income on housing, with particularly acute impacts in Boston and surrounding communities where displacement of long-time residents is increasing.
statements.policyBackground: Rent stabilization or rent control policies limit how much and how often landlords can raise rents on existing tenants, typically capping annual increases at a fixed percentage or inflation rate. Massachusetts voters banned rent control statewide in 1994, though some advocates seek to restore it. Proponents argue such policies prevent displacement and keep housing affordable, while opponents say they discourage new construction, reduce property maintenance, and create housing shortages.

james.quote: As Governor, I will declare a statewide housing emergency, create a Social Housing Authority to build permanently affordable housing, use state-owned land to build tens of thousands of homes, support rent stabilization policies, tie state housing funding to tenant protections, and tax luxury real estate speculation and large corporate landlords.

statements.text: Parental consent should be required for minors to receive gender-related medical treatments.

candidatePositions.james: James will codify protections for gender-affirming healthcare and strengthen anti-discrimination protections in housing, healthcare, employment, and education.

statements.raceInsight: LGBTQ rights, particularly for transgender individuals, have become increasingly prominent political issues in Massachusetts and nationwide, affecting healthcare access, school policies, and civil rights protections.
statements.policyBackground: Parental consent laws require that a parent or guardian approve medical care before it is provided to a minor. Gender-related medical treatments may include puberty blockers, hormone therapy, or surgical procedures. Supporters argue parents have the right and responsibility to make major medical decisions for their children.

james.quote: As governor, I will codify protections for gender-affirming healthcare and strengthen anti-discrimination protections. I will strengthen and enforce nondiscrimination protections in housing, healthcare, employment, and education, and ensure that state agencies are accountable when those protections are violated.

statements.text: Military aid to foreign countries should be conditioned on compliance with human rights standards.

candidatePositions.markey: Markey voted for resolutions to apply human rights provisions to U.S. aid to Israel and to cancel the Trump administration's sales of bombs and munitions to Israel.

statements.raceInsight: U.S. foreign policy in the Middle East matters to Massachusetts voters across diverse communities, including those with connections to Israel and Palestine, and those concerned about how tax dollars are spent abroad.
statements.policyBackground: The United States provides billions in military aid annually to other countries, with Israel historically receiving the largest share. Human rights conditions would make this aid contingent on the recipient country's treatment of civilians, compliance with international law, or other standards. Existing law includes some human rights provisions, but enforcement varies. Supporters argue conditions promote accountability and align aid with American values, while opponents say they undermine strategic alliances and national security interests.

markey.quote: In January 2024, Markey voted for a resolution proposed by Senator Bernie Sanders to apply the human rights provisions of the Foreign Assistance Act to U.S. aid to Israel's military. The proposal was defeated, 72 to 11. In April 2025, Markey voted for a pair of resolutions Sanders proposed to cancel the Trump administration's sales of $8.8 billion in bombs and other munitions to Israel.

statements.text: The state should invest in building new prison facilities.

candidatePositions.james: James plans to pause the process of designing and building a $360M women's prison and focus on reducing incarceration and implementing alternatives.

statements.raceInsight: Criminal justice reform and incarceration rates affect public safety, state budgets, and racial equity in Massachusetts, where advocates have pushed for alternatives to imprisonment while others emphasize law and order concerns.
statements.policyBackground: Prison construction involves building new correctional facilities or expanding existing ones to house incarcerated individuals. Decisions about prison construction relate to debates over appropriate incarceration levels, conditions of confinement, and whether to invest in jails versus alternatives like diversion programs, mental health treatment, or probation. New facilities require significant capital investment and ongoing operational costs, while proponents argue they may be necessary to address overcrowding or replace outdated infrastructure.

james.quote: Pause the process of designing and building a $360M women's prison and make time to focus on further reducing the number of people in jail and prison, and implement alternatives before building anything new.

statements.text: The state should ban the manufacturing of assault rifles.

healey.quote: On July 20, 2016, Healey announced her intention to ban the manufacturing of most assault rifles in Massachusetts.

candidatePositions.healey: Healey announced her intention to ban the manufacturing of most assault rifles in Massachusetts.

statements.raceInsight: Gun policy remains a significant issue in Massachusetts, where voters and policymakers debate how to balance public safety concerns with Second Amendment rights. The state already has some of the nation's strictest gun laws.
statements.policyBackground: Assault rifles, or assault weapons, are typically semi-automatic firearms with certain military-style features, though definitions vary by jurisdiction. Manufacturing bans prohibit companies from producing these weapons within a state's borders. Such bans are distinct from sales bans, possession bans, or federal regulations.

statements.text: Mandatory minimum sentences for drug offenses should be maintained or strengthened.

healey.quote: Healey's plan for criminal justice reform includes ending mandatory sentences for nonviolent drug offenders and focusing on treatment rather than incarceration.

candidatePositions.healey: Healey's criminal justice reform plan includes ending mandatory sentences for nonviolent drug offenders and focusing on treatment rather than incarceration.

statements.raceInsight: Criminal justice reform has gained attention in Massachusetts as policymakers consider alternatives to incarceration and address concerns about racial disparities in sentencing. The opioid crisis has particularly influenced debates about drug-related penalties.
statements.policyBackground: Mandatory minimum sentences require judges to impose a minimum prison term for certain drug offenses, regardless of individual circumstances. These sentencing laws remove judicial discretion in determining punishment. Supporters argue they provide consistency, deter crime, and ensure serious consequences for drug trafficking.

I will rescind the current administration's sales and use tax exemption for data centers.

james.stance: James plans to pause the process of designing and building a $360M women's prison and focus on reducing incarceration and implementing alternatives.
james.quote: Pause the process of designing and building a $360M women's prison and make time to focus on further reducing the number of people in jail and prison, and implement alternatives before building anything new.

james.stance: James opposes what she describes as genocide inflicted upon the Palestinian people by the State of Israel and opposes welcoming Israeli companies that have funded Israel to do business in Massachusetts.
james.quote: Our campaign stands in opposition to the genocide at the hands of the State of Israel and inflicted upon the Palestinian people. Our campaign stands in opposition to welcoming companies from Israel that have funded the State of Israel to carry out the genocide of the Palestinian people, to do business in Massachusetts.

james.stance: James supports and defends protests concerning Israel/Palestine and joins BDS campaigns to put pressure on Israel.
james.quote: We support and defend protests in the streets and on campuses, and we join BDS campaigns to put pressure on Israel.

james.stance: James will tax luxury real estate speculation and large corporate landlords to help finance housing construction.
james.quote: Housing construction will be financed through public capital bonding, progressive real estate taxation on luxury speculation and corporate landlords, and the use of state-owned land to reduce development costs.

sentences.text: Edward John Markey was born on July 11, 1946, in Malden, Massachusetts, the son of a milkman.
sentences.quote: Markey was born on July 11, 1946, in Malden, Massachusetts, the son of Christina M. (née Courtney) and John E. Markey, a milkman.

sentences.text: He graduated from Boston College in 1968 with a Bachelor of Arts and from Boston College Law School in 1972 with a Juris Doctor.
sentences.quote: Markey graduated from Boston College in 1968 with a Bachelor of Arts and from Boston College Law School in 1972 with a Juris Doctor.

sentences.text: After graduating, Markey worked as a lawyer in private practice and served in the United States Army Reserve from 1968 to 1973, attaining the rank of Specialist 4.
sentences.quote: After graduating, Markey worked as a lawyer in private practice. He served in the United States Army Reserve from 1968 to 1973, attaining the rank of Specialist 4.

sentences.text: He served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives from 1973 to 1976, then as U.S. representative for Massachusetts's 7th congressional district from 1976 to 2013.
sentences.quote: A member of the Democratic Party, he served 20 terms (18 full, two partial) as the U.S. representative for Massachusetts's 7th congressional district from 1976 to 2013. Before that, he was a member of the Massachusetts House of Representatives from 1973 to 1976.

sentences.text: In 2013, after John Kerry was appointed United States Secretary of State, Markey was elected to serve out the remainder of Kerry's Senate term in a special election and has served as junior United States senator from Massachusetts since 2013.
sentences.quote: In 2013, after John Kerry was appointed United States Secretary of State, Markey was elected to serve out the remainder of Kerry's Senate term in a 2013 special election.

sentences.text: For over twenty years, he has practiced law in Massachusetts and surrounding states, representing mesothelioma and cancer victims against Fortune 100 companies, and in 2006 he founded his own small law practice.
sentences.quote: For over twenty years, John has been practicing law in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and surrounding states, representing mesothelioma and cancer victims against Fortune 100 companies. sentences.text: Maura Tracy Healey was born on February 8, 1971, at Walter Reed Hospital, in Bethesda, Maryland, and was raised in Hampton Falls, New Hampshire.
sentences.quote: Healey was born on February 8, 1971, at Walter Reed Hospital, in Bethesda, Maryland. When she was nine months old, her family moved to Hampton Falls, New Hampshire, where she was raised.

sentences.text: After clerking for a federal judge, Healey spent more than seven years at the law firm Wilmer Cutler Pickering Hale and Dorr LLP, where she worked as an associate and then junior partner.
sentences.quote: Healey subsequently spent more than seven years at the law firm Wilmer Cutler Pickering Hale and Dorr LLP, where she worked as an associate and then junior partner and focused on commercial and securities litigation.

sentences.text: Hired by Massachusetts Attorney General Martha Coakley in 2007, Healey served as chief of the Civil Rights Division, then chief of the Public Protection and Advocacy Bureau, and then chief of the Business and Labor Bureau before resigning in 2013 to run for attorney general.
sentences.quote: Hired by Massachusetts Attorney General Martha Coakley in 2007, Healey served as chief of the Civil Rights Division, where she led the state's challenge to the federal Defense of Marriage Act. She was then appointed chief of the Public Protection and Advocacy Bureau and then chief of the Business and Labor Bureau, before resigning in 2013 to run for attorney general in 2014.

sentences.text: She served as Massachusetts Attorney General from 2015 to 2023 and has been serving as the 73rd governor of Massachusetts since 2023.
sentences.quote: Maura Tracy Healey (born February 8, 1971) is an American lawyer and politician serving as the 73rd governor of Massachusetts since 2023. A member of the Democratic Party, she served as Massachusetts Attorney General from 2015 to 2023 and was elected governor in 2022.

sentences.text: Andrea C. James was born and raised in Boston, Massachusetts.
sentences.quote: James was born and raised in Boston, Massachusetts.

sentences.text: She graduated with a bachelor's from University of Massachusetts, Boston and a Juris Doctor degree from Northeastern University, returning to Boston to work as a criminal defence and real estate conveyance attorney in Roxbury.
sentences.quote: She graduated with a bachelor's from University of Massachusetts, Boston and a Juris Doctor degree from Northeastern University, returning to Boston to work as a criminal defence and real estate conveyance attorney in Roxbury.

sentences.text: In 2009, she was sentenced to 24 months in federal prison on charges of wire fraud, and in 2010, James was formally disbarred by the Supreme Court of Suffolk County.
sentences.quote: In 2009, she was sentenced to 24 months in federal prison on charges of wire fraud. In 2010, James was formally disbarred by the Supreme Court of Suffolk County.

sentences.text: Following her release, James founded and served as the executive director of Families for Justice as Healing (FJAH), a non-governmental organisation that advocated for criminal justice reform.
sentences.quote: Following her release, James founded and served as the executive director of Families for Justice as Healing (FJAH), a non-governmental organisation that advocated for criminal justice reform through prioritising community wellness alternatives over incarceration.

sentences.text: In May 2025, James filed paperwork to run in 2026 as governor of Massachusetts as a Democrat.
sentences.quote: In May 2025, James filed paperwork to run in 2026 as governor of Massachusetts as a Democrat, stating to the Boston Globe she was "exploring" a run.
